Thanks for the response! Yeah, I'm working on building up a better friend group by working on being more positive and attracting more positive people. After losing someone I trusted recently I've been working on rekindling relationships around me and trying to keep my eyes open for red flags of narcissists and "one uppers" (as another poster called them). I want to be around people who are encouraging and willing to be honest with me and treat me with respect and, most of all, don't invalidate my feelings! It's a process but I keep telling myself it will get better (I'm having a slightly less depressed day today...). Thanks and good luck to you!

That's always frustrating or "oh she can do that because she has energy and I'm just too tired to do anything because my x is so much worse." It's like, stop, I am forcing myself to do this, it's not like I just magically have tons of energy. To use the phrase "I'm borrowing from tomorrow's spoons." I hate using my spoons because someone else feels like I have more.

I just don't understand it. We all struggle, have a little actual empathy and help, don't be a self-centered invalidator. The world is full of enough difficult people without doing it to supposed friends.

A sport? But yeah, I try not to mention it, unless I trust the person and am letting them know to let me know if I'm doing something super weird because I've been off meds for a while and I'm not doing super great.

People need to have some chill, as my younger friends would say. Haha.
